title: The Most Pseudoscientific Government in the World
description:
When India’s Prime Minister claimed that “superstitious people cannot bring development,” it sounded like a defense of science and reason. But history shows a very different story. From bizarre claims of plastic surgery in Ganesha’s trunk, to nuclear tests by sages, to yogic farming, cow urine cures, and internet in the Mahabharata, leaders of the ruling party have repeatedly replaced science with superstition.

This video traces some of the wildest pseudoscientific claims made by ministers, MPs, and even judges:

PM Modi saying Lord Ganesha was the first plastic surgery patient.
Ministers insisting astrology is superior to science.
Claims of ancient Indian aircrafts, stem-cell tech, and guided missiles thousands of years ago.
A High Court judge declaring that peacocks reproduce by drinking tears.
Education ministers pushing Pushpak Viman and gravity before Newton into school curricula.
Ministers calling cow urine a cancer cure and coronavirus a living being with rights.
The absurdity of 9 pm candle lighting, banging thalis, and “go corona go” chants during the pandemic.

We also examine the creation of the AYUSH ministry, which funnels public money into pseudosciences like Ayurveda, Homeopathy, Siddha, and Unani, while failing to produce peer-reviewed evidence for effectiveness.

If you’ve searched for Modi pseudoscience, BJP leaders fake science, Ganesha plastic surgery claim, internet in Mahabharata, or cow urine cancer cure, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Like, comment, share, and hype this video so more people see the absurdity of mixing superstition with governance.

Chapters 
00:00 – Intro: The PM vs Superstition
01:40 – Ganesha & Ancient Plastic Surgery
04:00 – Astrology “Above Science”
06:20 – Ancient Aircrafts & Nuclear Tests
08:40 – Peacocks, Pushpaks & Gravity
11:00 – Pseudoscience in the Pandemic
14:00 – AYUSH: The Pseudoscience Ministry
18:30 – Conclusion: Clean Your Own House
